meeting_header:
Date: 2027-12-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya V. (Redwood CSM), Rachel Kim (BrightFind Head of Search), Tom Baker (BrightFind Eng Manager), Nina Patel (BrightFind ML Engineer), Samir Rao (BrightFind Product)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked BrightFind through the hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints. Demo included embeddings generation, index/nearby search flow, and live rerank on a small product-search example. Customer concerned about latency at tail, data residency, and integration effort. Agreed to send pricing and security docs and scope a 2-week POC with benchmark script.
transcript:
00:00 Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. Quick intro from BrightFind?
00:10 Rachel: Hi, Rachel Kim, I run search at BrightFind. We own the product search stack. Tom and Nina here.
00:18 Tom: Hey all.
00:20 Nina: Hi.
00:22 Avery: Great. Goal for today is a short walkthrough of our hosted embeddings endpoint and the reranker - focus on search relevance improvements and what a POC would look like. We'll keep it practical.
00:35 Diego: I'll kick off with the architecture - very high level. You call the embeddings endpoint, get fixed-dim vectors, push into your vector index (we usually see Pinecone used, some folks use open source like Weaviate or OpenSearch dense vector). Then on search we do an initial ANN retrieval and optionally call our rerank endpoint which takes the query, doc text, and returns a relevance score or re-ranked list.
01:02 Rachel: Quick Q - do you host the vector index or is that customer-managed?
01:07 Avery: For hosted API the embeddings are generated by Redwood and you typically manage the vector store. For Dedicated we can host or provide managed index options via partners. For the quick POC we recommend you keep your existing index, we can work with Pinecone or your self-hosted OpenSearch.
01:20 Nina: What's the dimensionality for embeddings and how much control do we have?
01:25 Diego: Standard models we demo at 1024 or 1536 dims depending on model choice; you can pick model and dimensionality, and we return embeddings as float32 by default, but we support quantized formats and reduced precision for storage savings.
01:38 Rachel: Cool. Show us the live demo?
01:41 Avery: Yep. Diego, want to share the console and curl examples?
01:45 Diego: Sharing screen - demo deck link: https://redwood.ai/decks/brightfind-demo - I'm going to run a small flow: first create embedding for product title + description, insert placeholder into local index, run similarity query, then call rerank with top-k to improve ordering.
02:10 Diego: (typing) Okay, curl POST /v1/embeddings with body {"input":"leather wallet, black, RFID"} - response vector back. Quick note: the API returns embedding and metadata id, plus timing.
02:28 Avery: You might see minor transcription typos in the log - sometimes KV cache appears as K V cash in transcripts, so ignore that, ha.
02:36 Tom: When you say 'rerank', is that a model that consumes the full doc text? We're worried about cost if we have to send long product descriptions.
02:44 Diego: Good question. Rerank supports either a short doc excerpt or a concatenated input. For long docs we recommend a hybrid: pass the query and a trimmed snippet (title + key attributes) and include a sparse signal or pre-computed small embedding. That dramatically reduces token count. Also you can use our batch rerank endpoint to amortize cost across many candidates.
03:05 Nina: How about latency? Our SLAs need p99 < 200ms for search results.
03:12 Avery: Hosted defaults get you good median latencies - the p99 is trickier and depends on batching and document size. For p99 < 200ms we usually recommend Dedicated capacity or pin a lower-latency model variant and enable prefix/KV caching. Diego can show some benchmark numbers we collected.
03:28 Diego: Yep, we ran a small benchmark with product-search-like payloads: embeddings (~5-15ms), ANN query depends on index, rerank per candidate ~30-120ms depending on model and token length. With batching and a trimmed input we got steady p95 ~120ms and p99 ~210-230ms on hosted; Dedicated reduced that p99 to under 180ms in our tests.
04:00 Rachel: Does Redwood provide a managed cache to avoid recomputing embeddings?
04:05 Diego: We support prefix and KV caching on the runtime side - e.g., for chat KV cache; but for embeddings you can cache in your vector store or use our SDK client-side caching patterns. We can provide recommendations in the Optimize tab in the console.
04:18 Samir: Any concerns about data residency? We have EU-only data for some catalogs.
04:22 Avery: For EU residency we can route calls to EU regions in the hosted product. If you need stricter isolation, Private or Dedicated in your VPC is the way to go. We'll attach the VPC deployment checklist in the follow-ups.
04:38 Diego: Back to demo - I'm doing a local similarity search, here's top-10, but quality is meh with raw vector scoring. Now calling the rerank endpoint POST /v1/rerank with the query and the top-10 docs.
04:55 Diego: Rerank returns a score array and we re-sort; you'll see better ordering especially for synonyms and intent. Example: 'wallet with RFID' previously returned clutch products; rerank prioritized products with 'RFID blocking' in features.
05:15 Rachel: Nice. Can we pass product metadata (price, availability) to rerank so it factors non-text signals?
05:21 Diego: Yes - the rerank payload supports per-candidate metadata fields and the scoring function can be configured to incorporate those features as priors. You can also run a post-sort that factors business logic.
05:34 Tom: For throughput - if we have 500 qps at peak, what's the recommended architecture?
05:40 Diego: For embeddings-only traffic that's heavier on the index; for rerank-heavy pipelines you can run an initial ANN to reduce candidate set to 10-20, then fan-out to rerank. For 500 qps we'd recommend Dedicated or a hybrid: hosted for low-volume/new queries, Dedicated pool for sustained peak. Autoscaling policies help smooth bursts.
06:05 Nina: How invasive is integration? We have a microservices search stack in Go.
06:09 Avery: The integration surface is minimal: call embeddings endpoint to upsert vectors, call search as you do today, optionally call rerank. We have Go and Python SDKs, and examples in the repo. We'll share a quickstarter template.
06:22 Diego: (shares code snippet) Example Go snippet: client.Embeddings.Create(...). Then index.Upsert(...). For rerank we send the candidate list and get back scores.
06:35 Rachel: Security - SSO, audit logs, encryption at rest?
06:40 Avery: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and encrypted data at rest using KMS. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
06:55 Samir: Who owns model updates? Like if you roll model versions, how is that handled during POC?
07:01 Diego: You choose model version and pin it on your route. We offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback to compatible variants if a newer model regresses. For POC we'll recommend pinning to a stable model.
07:18 Rachel: Any examples of quantization or cost controls for large catalogs?
07:22 Diego: Yes - Optimize tab gives quantization recommendations per workload, and we can suggest a 4-bit quantized model for embeddings storage, plus batching config to reduce token cost on rerank. We've seen 30-50% unit cost savings with modest latency impact.
07:38 Nina: Could you share the benchmark script and a small sample dataset?
07:42 Diego: Absolutely - action item, will drop a script and a sample 2k-product CSV.
07:48 Avery: Let's run a quick live rerank example with a slightly longer text to show token impact.
07:55 Diego: (runs longer example) You might see slightly higher latency - 170-220ms range for this particular request. Note that transcripts sometimes spell model names weirdly, like 'red wood' vs Redwood in captions.
08:15 Tom: Are there any rate limits we should be aware of?
08:18 Avery: Hosted has tiered rate limits; for POCs we can bump quotas. For production at scale, Dedicated is recommended.
08:25 Rachel: What's typical POC length and success criteria?
08:29 Avery: Usually 2-4 weeks. Success criteria commonly: measurable relevance lift in clicks/CTR or NDCG on a held-out set, acceptable p99 latency, and integration with your infra.
08:40 Samir: Budget constraints - what's ballpark pricing for this?
08:44 Avery: I'll send a hosted pricing matrix and Dedicated reserved pricing. We'll also include example unit economics - tokens per rerank, embedding storage cost, estimated index storage.
08:55 Nina: For rerank cost control if we do 10 candidates per query, any tips?
08:59 Diego: Use a cheaper rerank model for most queries and only escalate to a larger model for high-value queries. Also use pre-filters and metadata to reduce candidate churn.
09:15 Rachel: Ok let's summarize next steps.
09:18 Avery: Recap - we'll send pricing + security docs, Diego will provide the benchmark script and sample dataset, BrightFind will share logs/schema and confirm stakeholders/timeline. We'll set a POC scoping call week of Dec 20.
09:32 Tom: Sounds good.
09:35 Nina: Thanks.
09:36 Avery: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email and attach the deck and links.
09:40 (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some ASR artifacts present (mis-spelled proper nouns, occasional merged words). References: demo deck https://redwood.ai/decks/brightfind-demo, sample benchmark repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks (link provided for POC assets).
